The Swift binary is a SKELETON (RULE #1): it ships a clamped tempo-heuristic fallback and reads THIS file at runtime for the real genre feel. Zero-rebuild to tune. Schema owner: LoopStarGenrePack.swift.
name: Boom-Bap
blurb: 90s boom-bap: a dusty MPC-swung kick+snare, a rootless Rhodes sample-flip chopped into stabs, a pedal sub, and a lonesome sax line.

flavors.label: Dusty Vamp
flavors.blurb: One m7 chord chopped into MPC stabs and left to loop forever.

flavors.label: Dorian Flip
flavors.blurb: The classic i-IV dorian two-chord pocket, swung hard off the grid.

flavors.label: Jazz Flip
flavors.blurb: Pete Rock territory: a borrowed ii-V and maj7 loops, lush and rolling.

flavors.label: Grimy
flavors.blurb: Mobb Deep cold: strip the jazz color out and hit it bare and hard.

flavors.label: Lo-Fi Drift
flavors.blurb: No chops at all: a warped Rhodes pad drifting behind the beat.

arranger.llmStyleBrief: Boom-bap harmony is a two-bar sample loop that never resolves. Dorian and aeolian dominate; the tonic is m7 or m9 and stays put. Movement is i-IV, i-bVII, or a ii-V lifted whole from a jazz record. Voice it rootless, because the sub owns the root. Avoid functional cadences and clean pop turnarounds.
